capabilities: insert time tracker code blocks into notes via command
start, stop, edit, and delete tracked time entries
persist timer timestamps so tracking continues across Obsidian restarts
export tracked time as Markdown table, CSV, JSON, or PDF
expose a JS API for scripts such as Dataview
extras: README documents a known rendering flicker issue when modifying timekeep blocks, caused by Obsidian re-rendering the code block; PDFs are generated locally with pdfmake.
intentEvidence: heavily inspired by ObsidianSimpleTimeTracker (semi backwards compatible; some simple-time-tracker blocks can be renamed to timekeep)
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to track time spent on tasks inside notes and export that time data.

relations.evidence: heavily inspired by ObsidianSimpleTimeTracker (semi backwards compatible; some simple-time-tracker blocks can be renamed to timekeep)
exposes a JS API which can be used by other scripts such as with Dataview

summary: Time tracking plugin that inserts code-block timers in notes, keeps running across sessions, and exports tracked time as Markdown tables, CSV, JSON, or PDF.
